units.translation: 242-43. "Where such a throng": the word "where" is not used correctly; for it indicates place. It should have said "whither." And "he casts" is used for "he sends." He calls Thessaly "Panachaean," because it was first called Achaea after Achaeus, son of Xuthus.
5 Strabo IX 436 | sch. Hes. Scut. 70 | Et. M. 646, 39 | Eust. 327, 21 | 12 Hesych. ποῖ | Συν. ποῖ (Phot. Suid.)
13 ποῖ Platt : ποῦ | 15 ἐκλήθη Ἀχαία in P (cf. Deicke 17) : τῆς Ἀχαίας in L : τῆς 〈Ἑλλάδος〉 Ἀχαία in K in adn.
244. "May they destroy with fire": may they burn up, may they subdue in war, may they overturn. "Houses" means the land, the earth, by synecdoche.

246a. "But not escapable are the paths": but the road is not avoidable for them, for it is by necessity; nor is the contest without accomplishment, for they will accomplish it easily, as it were easy to succeed; [or thus] so that the meaning is: but not to be fled from, as it were impossible for them not to fulfill the command, 〈...〉.
20 εὐκατόρθωτος Fr. : -ορθώτως in L | deleted by Fr., referring the words οὐκ εὔπλοα which follow in the manuscripts to sch. b after οἱ δὲ οὕτως | 21 lacuna indicated by W

b. "And the toil not unaccomplished for those who go": the negative is common, so that it is: but not escapable are the paths, nor is the toil unaccomplished, but on the same day may they destroy the house of Aeetes with destructive fire, unless he willingly gives them the fleece. Others thus: 〈not escapable〉 not easy to sail 〈and〉 unaccomplished, hard to accomplish, hard to work, hard to succeed.
25 〈οὐ φ.〉 supplied by F | 〈καὶ〉 supplied by Fr.

247-49a. 〈But the women:〉 this too is in accordance with feminine nature. He has marvelously adapted the natures and speeches to both. For to the men, since their nature is bolder, he introduces accomplishment and fulfillment of what is to come, but for the women, since they are weaker, he makes prayers and supplications. For such are women in great and fearful matters.
1 sch. a in the manuscripts adheres to scholion b | 2 ἀμφοτέροις in L : -ων (in P)

251-52. "Wretched Alcimede": toil-worn. The sense: even if late, nevertheless evil came also to you, Alcimede. The preposition "through" is missing; and you did not continue your life splendidly, boasting in such a son.
10 αὐχοῦσα in F : -ωσα in L : differently in P
254-55a. 〈If formerly:〉 [or "was to him"] before the contest came upon him. "Of evils" either of his own or of those about to be accomplished by the Argonauts.
11 lemmata transposed by W following cod. Pal. 150
b. "With funeral offerings": with burial gifts. Lg (P)
